title: Greedy Best-First in Reykjavík: Stormy Routes!
description: Watch how Greedy Best-First navigates Reykjavík street-map graphs by always chasing the most promising next node. The visualization highlights how heuristic-driven choices can be fast—but not always optimal.
ig_caption:
🌍📍 Reykjavík (Miðborg) street-map search with **Greedy Best-First** ⚡

In graph terms, we model the road network as a weighted graph (streets = edges, intersections = nodes). **Greedy Best-First** selects the next node using only the heuristic, typically **h(n)=estimated distance to the goal** (like straight-line distance on real map geometry), without caring about the accumulated cost g(n). ✅ That means it often races toward the destination fast—but can miss the globally shortest path because it doesn’t balance *cost-so-far + estimated remaining distance*.

🧠 In this reel, notice the frontier behavior: the algorithm expands the most “goal-looking” nodes first, so the route shape is heavily guided by the heuristic’s accuracy on real-world street layouts. 🗺️
